subject: Repository ontology landscape, Invoke package, and continuation boundaries
why_now: Invoke crossed the durable-package threshold and exposed a repository-wide navigation problem: candidate models, governed packages, run receipts, UI projections, experiments, proofs, generated mirrors, and legacy ontology material were easy to confuse. This notice consolidates their current roles, entrypoints, validation posture, and owner gates without changing authority.
key_points: The current private model root is cyberAlchemy-v2/ontology. It is a candidate authority-model boundary: it can model authority, branches, nodes, relations, lifecycle, projections, and promotion requests, but it cannot decide or move authority.

The public reusable route is Arcanum: ontology-vault owns selection, mapping, materialization, validation, confidence and drift behavior; ontology-harness composes Inventory, Ontology Vault, and Context Builder. Inventory entries remain read models, not ontology authority.

Ontology Vault now distinguishes a one-off run artifact from a durable package. Stable identity, reuse, enrichment, multiple branches or views, bridge behavior, source bindings, schemas, or reusable projections require a package and fail closed when owner, root, or visibility is unresolved.

Invoke is now a candidate public package at arcanum/ontology/invoke. Its validated material digest is 094b52ac70444484ef9e46f812e7a460f619c71f4a2fa1ce40c2bf49f261ae6d. It preserves 9 business nodes, 9 system nodes, 8 business relations, 12 system relations, 9 bridge relations, 5 active and 2 deferred operations, 45 phases, 11 supporting capabilities, 14 public source bindings, and 11 residue items.
The three flat .arcanum Invoke JSON files remain byte-identical migration evidence, not product ontology state stores. The private migration receipt records their exact hashes and export checks.

The owner-approved CAV2-to-Arcanum boundary permits only sanitized ontology definition and model contracts. CAV2 proofs, executable scripts, private paths and digests, source evidence, and content from other systems are forbidden in public Arcanum bytes. Ontology and validation retain authority_effect none.

Current private project packages include Body War business and whole-system, Augmentor unified-agent, Anime.js agent-knowledge-vault and its operational library, Auth User Management domain ontology, and Lucifer's Lights Whisper ontology. DomainSpec v2 currently supplies a candidate instantiation boundary plus a separate architecture-property experiment, not one consolidated validated package.

UI and workbench surfaces are projections, not ontology owners: the CAV2 Ontology Evidence Workbench, candidate graph prototype, DomainSpec v2 architecture canvases and unified canvas planning package, Body War UI black-box evidence, Augmentor visualization, the older DomainSpec explorer, and the ontology authority presentation must retain their own candidate or historical claim ceilings.

No standalone Poker Team ontology package was found. Poker Team appears as bounded fixture/source evidence in the CAV2 workbench and candidate graph prototype; validation/poker-team is a product/runtime surface, not ontology authority.

Other relevant incubators and research lanes include projects/ontology, Ontologize operational ontology, CyberAlchemy Lab tower evidence ontology, Co-op Engine Whisper ontology runtime research, machine-map ontology operationalization, Akashic frontend ontology work, and the ontology dialect and stable-version research tracks.

Proof bodies, executable bodies, task-session and refresh staging copies, dist assets, generated run bundles, output mirrors, cleanup backups, and imported House Project conversations are excluded from the current-package inventory. They may be used only through their owning evidence route; their presence does not create another ontology package.

Legacy or ownership-unclear surfaces include cyberAlchemy/ontology, older CyberAlchemy operational ontology slices, implementation/domainspec vault ontology prose, the older DomainSpec explorer, Arcanum extraction research, and generated download archives. Do not treat these as current CAV2 authority or independent package roots.

open_calls.question: Should the validated arcanum/ontology/invoke candidate be accepted into an Invoke lifecycle and separately authorized for publication, without changing its authority_effect none posture?
Should cyberAlchemy-v2/ontology gain a package-level validator and immutable validation receipt for its current candidate model contracts?
Should projects/domainspec-v2/ontology remain a boundary-only instantiation surface or be materialized as a populated, validated DomainSpec v2 package?
Should Poker Team remain fixture-only evidence or receive its own owner-routed ontology package? No package exists today.
Should a governed repository-level package registry be created to index current roots, validators, receipts, visibility, authority posture, projections, and legacy exclusions?
Which lifecycle statement is current for projects/ontologize/operational-ontology, whose README says both executed end-to-end and run the route?

boundaries: This Handoff Notice is communication evidence only. It does not promote, publish, deploy, release, accept, or redefine any ontology, capability, project, proof, or runtime.

Only arcanum is public. CyberAlchemy v2, DomainSpec, projects, implementation, validation products, research, proof evidence, and operations material remain private unless a separate owner route authorizes a bounded export.

The public CAV2 export is limited to sanitized ontology definition and model contracts. Never copy CAV2 proofs, executable scripts, private source evidence, private paths or digests, or other-system content into Arcanum.
A package validator may be public when it is authored for and owned by that public package; this does not authorize exporting a private CAV2 script.
Ontology models authority but does not decide it. Every mapped or validated surface retains authority_effect none unless its separate owner route performs an authorized movement.

UI, visualization, canvas, workbench, presentation, and generated graph surfaces are projections over ontology or evidence; they are not ontology, definition, schema, or lifecycle authority by proximity.
Inventory entries, .arcanum run outputs, validation receipts, handoff notices, and migration receipts are evidence/read-model surfaces, not durable ontology state stores.
Generated skill mirrors, staged task copies, refresh snapshots, dist assets, proof copies, and output mirrors are not independent sources of truth. Resolve their canonical source before mutation.
Poker Team is currently source and fixture evidence only. Do not call it a standalone ontology package without a root, owner, profile, manifest, validator, and receipt.
The repository was dirty before this work. Preserve unrelated user-owned changes and revalidate exact current bytes before any later acceptance, promotion, publication, commit, or push.

next_actions.action: Review arcanum/ontology/invoke, its validation receipt, and private migration receipt; decide acceptance and any later publication through a separate owner gate.

Use this notice as the initial routing map, then validate current package roots before creating any repository-level registry. Keep model, package, projection, proof, generated mirror, and legacy classifications separate.
Decide whether the CAV2 model root needs a deterministic package validator and immutable receipt; do not infer authority movement from validation.

next_actions.owner: DomainSpec v2 and Poker Team owners
next_actions.action: Resolve whether their current boundary or fixture surfaces should materialize into owned packages; do not grow existing experiment or UI receipts into package state.
Bind each active projection to its exact source graph, adapter receipt, validation command, and candidate or historical status before calling it current.
Re-run Ontology Vault validation and repository discovery from current bytes; use proof and script locations only through their owning routes and preserve the public/private boundary.
